Maya R: Heads-up — prep for the 'Inference Claims' refresh. Marketing needs a tight rebut guide vs cloud providers + LLM API players. Can we get a quick sync today?
Sanjay Patel: +1, we should bake in the new benchmark numbers (latency P50/P95 + token cost). Quick ask: which stat is most defensible right now?
Tess Nguyen: Use P95 latency and steady-state token $/1k as the core. Ops teams validated batch savings on Dedicated; we can call out ~32% cost reduction on long-tail prompts.
Ben Cho: Got the cost calc, will drop a short table. Important: avoid absolute “faster” claims unless we cite specific model configs. Focus on predictable latency and routing fallbacks.
Marco Li: Also call out Private (VPC) + KMS as a procurement win vs public cloud endpoints. Sales asked for one-liner for security decks.
Maya R: Draft one-liner idea: "Production-first inference: predictable latency, transparent unit economics, and deployment flexibility (hosted, dedicated, private)." Thoughts?
Tess Nguyen: Nice — maybe shorter: "Predictable latency. Predictable cost. Deploy where you need to."
Sanjay Patel: Love that. For battlecard sections we need: 1) Quick claim vs Cloud AI 2) Quick claim vs LLM APIs 3) Objection handlers 4) Suggested demo prompts 5) Competitive signals to watch.
Ben Cho: Objection handler snippet for cost: `If you see lower sticker price from X, ask about long-tail token inflation, prefix reuse, and prefix cache capabilities.`
Maya R: Add a short script for SDRs: "If customer asks about managed endpoints, highlight SLA, burst capacity, and kernel-level optimizations that reduce tail latency."
comp-bot: Deploy note: updated benchmark blob uploaded -> https://redwood-internal/benchmarks/2026-03-inference-vs-cloud.csv :ledger:  
Marco Li: Thanks @comp-bot. I pulled the CSV — P95 numbers look solid on T4/T4p sim. We should include an A/B phrasing: "When latency matters, choose dedicated pools; when elasticity matters, choose hosted."
Tess Nguyen: Webinar angle: run a 30-min live demo showing identical prompt hitting hosted vs dedicated vs private (with diff routing). Title idea: "Serving the Real World: Cost, Latency, and Reliability at Scale"
Sanjay Patel: Love that. Add a 10-min Q/A about procurement/security. Ask: who will own the demo infra? Eng-runtime team? @Marco Li @Ben Cho can coordinate.
Ben Cho: I can stand up the demo harness. Will need a short SOP for metrics collection + a canned prompt set (5 prompts: short chat, instruction, long context, retrieval-augmented, code completion).
Maya R: For the battlecard's quick rebuts — short bullets only. Example: 
- Claim: "Cloud provider X is cheaper." 
  Rebuttal: "Unit economics depend on batch strategy and cache reuse; here's our typical delta for conv workloads: ~30% lower cost at scale."
- Claim: "Managed LLM APIs are easier."
  Rebuttal: "True for prototypes; for production you need SLAs, rollout controls, and predictable scaling — all first-class in Redwood."
Tess Nguyen: Can we add a 2-line technical footnote for sales: mention KV-cache, continuous batching, and quantization path to justify cost claims.
Sanjay Patel: Yes. Keep footnote non-technical but specific: e.g., "Prefix KV cache + continuous batching reduce per-token work by avoiding repeated compute on warm prefixes."
Maya R: Action items: Ben -> demo harness + metrics SOP (due EOD tomorrow). Marco -> short security one-pager for procurement (due +2 days). Tess -> draft battlecard bullets + A/B phrases (due EOD). Sanjay -> compile benchmark highlights + 2-slide appendix for webinar (due tomorrow noon). I'll assemble the doc and share for review.
Ben Cho: On it. Will ping when demo infra ready. :thumbsup:
Marco Li: Will draft KMS/VC documentation.
Tess Nguyen: Drafting bullets now, linking here when done.
Maya R: Great — if anyone has a hard objection line they want included, drop it here. We need this to be slimmest possible rebut sheet for SDRs.
Sanjay Patel: One more: include a short procurement-friendly table comparing commitments (hosted usage, dedicated reserved capacity, private licensing + support). Helps procurement triage.
Maya R: Perfect. Final ask — keep all messaging neutral vs named competitors; use categories like "cloud AI providers" or "managed LLM APIs". We'll add competitor-specific notes in a separate internal doc.
Tess Nguyen: Understood. Posting draft in 45m.
comp-bot: Reminder set: review meeting scheduled in 1 day -> #marketing-review 2026-03-25 10:00
